messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike in prod-us-west-2 for inference-route /v1/generate. p99 jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.8s starting ~04:32 UTC. Auto-scaling not tripping. Possible kernel/quantization deploy overlap. Paging signs in node logs. @eng-oncall please triage.

Priya Desai: I'm on it. Which deploys landed around that window? Any rollout IDs?

Alex Kim: Rolling update of runtime image `redwood-runtime:trt8-quant-2026-03-15` finished ~04:30 UTC. It included TRT8 + FlashAttn build and a quant kernel change (enable 4-bit fused kernels). I suspect the new NV kernel path.

Jordan Lee: Confirming saw a tail increase on streaming sessions too — streaming stalls and tail p99 for token decode up across pools. Linking quick graphs: https://grafana.redwood/intern/dashboards/p99-decode (perm: eng)

SRE-Bot: p95: 280ms -> 520ms, p99: 220ms -> 1840ms, error rate steady. Topos show elevated memcpy stalls and rare page-fault backoff in /var/log/nvkernel.log.

Marta Alvarez: Paging lines in kernel logs (snippet):
```
[04:32:12] nv_kernel: backoff on kernel page fault, fallback sw-kv-cache
[04:32:13] loader: mapped pages 0x7f8a.. -> slow path
[04:32:14] runtime: disable_prefetch_hint=false
```
This looks like a new path in the quant kernel triggers slower path for long sequences.

Alex Kim: If it's the fused quant kernel we shipped, that could change memory access patterns & KV prefetch. Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback runtime image to previous tag, 2) flip runtime flag to force legacy decode kernel (ENV: USE_LEGACY_DECODER=true), 3) pin models to dedicated non-quant variant. I recommend rollback + flag if rollback takes time.

Priya Desai: Agreed. I'll trigger a targeted rollback on the small fleet first (canary group) to validate.

Priya Desai: @deploy-bot rollback job started: target=prod-us-west-2-canary, from=redwood-runtime:trt8-quant-2026-03-15 -> to=redwood-runtime:trt8-2026-03-10. Job id: rb-20260315-33

Ken Liu: I'm checking node-level metrics. There's an uptick in kernel NVTE cache misses and memcpy latency on gpus with >16k sequence; short seqs look mostly unaffected.

Jordan Lee: Running a synthetic perf check on a sample worker (command):
```
# run playback for seq=4096 tokens
python tools/playback_perf.py --model redwood-1.3b --seq 4096 --concurrency 4 --endpoint localhost:8080
# before: p99 ~210ms, after deploy: p99 ~1.7s
```

Marta Alvarez: I'm trying the ENV flip on one node via `kubectl exec` into runtime pod to set `USE_LEGACY_DECODER=true` and restart process. Will report perf delta.

Alex Kim: Also check the compile flags we built with: `-DUSE_FLASHATTN=1 -DQUANT_FUSED=1 -O3 -fno-fast-math` — if fused quant uses larger working set, we might be hitting kernel path that pages. There's a flag to disable KV prefetch on the newer kernels: `KV_PREFETCH=0` (we didn't expose it in the rollout, Alex added it to the next image). If immediate rollback isn't clean, flipping KV_PREFETCH could help.

Priya Desai: Canary rollback completed -> verification: p99 on canary workers dropped from 1.8s -> 230ms within ~2 minutes. Good signal.

IncidentBot: Rollback event detected: rb-20260315-33 SUCCESS on prod-us-west-2-canary. Notifying rollout monitor.

Priya Desai: I'm proceeding with a staged rollback across the fleet. Rolling groups 2/6 now. ETA full rollback ~12 minutes if steady.

Jordan Lee: While rollback continues, collect kernel logs from impacted nodes (commands):
```
kubectl logs runtime-pod-xyz -c nv-kernel | grep -i "backoff\|page fault\|prefetch"
scp user@node:/var/log/nvkernel.log ./nvkernel-node-xyz.log
```

Marta Alvarez: Flip attempt (USE_LEGACY_DECODER) on a non-canary pod showed p99 drop to ~250ms but some sessions reported minor regressions in throughput (expected). Good test though.

Ken Liu: Noted a handful of customers reported increased latency in Intercom (CS ticket #78923). Customer impact: elevated latency causing slow UI autocompletes for a small set of heavy-seq requests. No errors or dropped requests observed.

Priya Desai: Customer impact note added to incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/2026-03-15-quant-kernel-p99 (internal). Please add any customer-facing bullets if we need to notify.

Alex Kim: Root cause hypothesis: Fused 4-bit quant kernel introduced altered memory-access stride causing frequent page fault fallback when KV cache grows beyond threshold. This surfaces for long-seq streaming workloads and triggers slow path memory copies in the kernel. Workaround: rollback or force legacy decode path. Long-term: tune fused kernel memory layout and add a runtime guard to fall back earlier to a low-working-set variant.

Priya Desai: Full rollback finished across prod-us-west-2 at +18 minutes. p99 returned to baseline across regions. Rolling update halted for the day.

SRE-Bot: Incident summary: duration ~18m, p99 spike to ~1.8s, impacted streaming tail and long-seq decode. Mitigation: staged rollback to previous runtime image. No request errors, limited customer UX impact. Postmortem assigned.

Priya Desai: Assigning postmortem: owners Alex Kim + Marta Alvarez. Action items:
- [ ] capture kernel logs from affected nodes
- [ ] add automated Canary perf test for long-sequence streaming
- [ ] expose KV_PREFETCH toggle in runtime config
- [ ] add regression alert for p99 delta >3x on decode

Alex Kim: I'll open a patch to disable fused quant kernel by default and add a perf gate on rollout. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4529

Jordan Lee: Handoff: I'm on-call for the next 6 hours, will monitor graphs and customer tickets. @Priya please ping if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

Priya Desai: Thanks team. Handoff notes: rollback successful, postmortem owners assigned, customer impact logged, follow-ups in the postmortem. Handing to @Jordan. /end
